package game.map;

import game.map.cells.Cell;
import game.map.cells.FillableCell;
import game.map.cells.TerminationCell;
import game.map.cells.Wall;
import game.pipes.Pipe;
import io.Deserializer;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import util.Coordinate;
import util.Direction;
import util.StringUtils;

import java.util.*;

/**
 * Map of the game.
 */
public class Map {

	private final int rows;
	private final int cols;
	@NotNull
	final Cell[][] cells;

	private TerminationCell sourceCell;
	private TerminationCell sinkCell;

	@NotNull
	private final Set<Coordinate> filledTiles = new HashSet<>();
	private int prevFilledTiles = 0;
	private Integer prevFilledDistance;

	/**
	 * Constructs a map from a map string.
	 * <p>
	 * This is a convenience method for unit testing.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param rows     Number of rows.
	 * @param cols     Number of columns.
	 * @param cellsRep String representation of the map, with columns delimited by {@code '\n'}.
	 * @return A map with the cells set from {@code cellsRep}.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException If the map is incorrectly formatted.
	 */
	@NotNull
	static Map fromString(int rows, int cols, @NotNull String cellsRep) {
		var cells = Deserializer.parseString(rows, cols, cellsRep);

		return new Map(rows, cols, cells);
	}

	/**
	 * Tries to place a pipe at (row, col).
	 *
	 * @param coord Coordinate to place pipe at.
	 * @param pipe  Pipe to place in cell.
	 * @return {@code true} if the pipe is placed in the cell, {@code false} otherwise.
	 */
	public boolean tryPlacePipe(@NotNull final Coordinate coord, @NotNull final Pipe pipe) {
		return tryPlacePipe(coord.row, coord.col, pipe);
	}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateStartCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			int row = rng.nextInt(rows);
			int col = rng.nextInt(cols);
			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			int dir = rng.nextInt(4);
			direction = Direction.values()[dir];

			if (row == 0 || row == rows - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			if (col == 0 || col == cols - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			switch (direction) {
			case UP:
				if (row <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case DOWN:
				if (row >= rows - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case LEFT:
				if (col <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case RIGHT:
				if (col >= cols - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateEndCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			// false -> X-axis, true -> Y-axis
			boolean axisToClamp = rng.nextInt(2) == 1;
			int row = axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? rows - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(rows - 2) + 1;
			int col = !axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? cols - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(cols - 2) + 1;

			if (row == col) {
				continue;
			}

			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			if (axisToClamp) {
				if (row == 0) {
					direction = Direction.UP;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.DOWN;
				}
			} else {
				if (col == 0) {
					direction = Direction.LEFT;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.RIGHT;
				}
			}

			var adjacentCell = coord.add(direction.getOpposite().getOffset());
			if (adjacentCell.equals(sourceCell.coord)) {
				continue;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	/**
	 * Displays the current map.
	 */
	public void display() {
		final int padLength = Integer.valueOf(rows - 1).toString().length();

		Runnable printColumns = () -> {
			System.out.print(StringUtils.createPadding(padLength, ' '));
			System.out.print(' ');
			for (int i = 0; i < cols - 2; ++i) {
				System.out.print((char) ('A' + i));
			}
			System.out.println();
		};

		printColumns.run();

		for (int i = 0; i < rows; ++i) {
			if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1) {
				System.out.print(String.format("%1$" + padLength + "s", i));
			} else {
				System.out.print(StringUtils.createPadding(padLength, ' '));
			}

			Arrays.stream(cells[i]).forEachOrdered(elem -> System.out.print(elem.toSingleChar()));

			if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1) {
				System.out.print(i);
			}

			System.out.println();
		}

		printColumns.run();
	}

	public void fillBeginTile() {
		sourceCell.setFilled();
	}

	public void Map(int rows, int cols) {
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
				cells[r][c] = new FillableCell();
			}
		}
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sourceInfo = generateStartCellInfo();
		Coordinate sourceCoord = sourceInfo.coord;
		Direction sourceDirection = sourceInfo.direction;
		sourceCell = new TerminationCell(sourceCoord, sourceDirection, true);
		cells[sourceCoord.row][sourceCoord.col] = sourceCell;
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sinkInfo = generateEndCellInfo();
		Coordinate sinkCoord = sinkInfo.coord;
		Direction sinkDirection = sinkInfo.direction;
		sinkCell = new TerminationCell(sinkCoord, sinkDirection, false);
		cells[sinkCoord.row][sinkCoord.col] = sinkCell;
	}

	public void Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) {
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			System.arraycopy(cells[r], 0, this.cells[r], 0, cols);
		}
		sourceCell = null;
		sinkCell = null;
		int sourceCount = 0;
		int sinkCount = 0;
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
				Cell cell = this.cells[r][c];
				if (cell instanceof TerminationCell termCell) {
					if (termCell.isSource()) {
						sourceCount++;
						sourceCell = termCell;
						if (r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source must not be on edge");
						}
						Direction dir = termCell.getDirection();
						Coordinate nextCoord = new Coordinate(r, c).add(dir.getOffset());
						if (isInBounds(nextCoord)) {
							Cell nextCell = this.cells[nextCoord.row][nextCoord.col];
							if (nextCell instanceof Wall) {
								throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source cannot point into a wall");
							}
						}
					} else {
						if (r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1) {
							sinkCount++;
							sinkCell = termCell;
							Direction dir = termCell.getDirection();
							Coordinate nextCoord = new Coordinate(r, c).add(dir.getOffset());
							if (isInBounds(nextCoord)) {
								throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink must point outside the map");
							}
						}
					}
				}
			}
		}
		if (sourceCount != 1) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("There must be exactly one source cell");
		}
		if (sinkCount != 1) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("There must be exactly one sink cell");
		}
	}

	boolean tryPlacePipe(int row, int col, Pipe p) {
		int r = row - 1;
		int c = col - 1;
		if (r < 0 || r >= rows || c < 0 || c >= cols) {
			return false;
		}
		Cell targetCell = cells[r][c];
		if (targetCell instanceof FillableCell fillable && !fillable.isOccupied()) {
			fillable.setPipe(p);
			return true;
		}
		return false;
	}

	public void undo(final Coordinate coord) {
		int r = coord.row;
		int c = coord.col;
		if (!isInBounds(coord)) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Coordinate out of bounds");
		}
		Cell currentCell = cells[r][c];
		if (!(currentCell instanceof FillableCell)) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cell is not fillable");
		}
		cells[r][c] = new FillableCell();
		filledTiles.remove(coord);
	}

	public void fillTiles(int distance) {
		if (sourceCell == null) {
			return;
		}
		filledTiles.clear();
		Queue<Coordinate> queue = new LinkedList<>();
		Map<Coordinate, Integer> distanceMap = new HashMap<>();
		Coordinate start = sourceCell.coord;
		queue.offer(start);
		distanceMap.put(start, 0);
		filledTiles.add(start);
		cells[start.row][start.col].setFilled();
		while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
			Coordinate current = queue.poll();
			int currentDist = distanceMap.get(current);
			if (currentDist >= distance) {
				continue;
			}
			for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
				Coordinate neighbor = current.add(dir.getOffset());
				if (isInBounds(neighbor) && !filledTiles.contains(neighbor)) {
					Cell neighborCell = cells[neighbor.row][neighbor.col];
					if (!(neighborCell instanceof Wall)) {
						neighborCell.setFilled();
						filledTiles.add(neighbor);
						distanceMap.put(neighbor, currentDist + 1);
						queue.offer(neighbor);
					}
				}
			}
		}
	}

	public boolean checkPath() {
		if (sourceCell == null || sinkCell == null) {
			return false;
		}
		Set<Coordinate> visited = new HashSet<>();
		Queue<Coordinate> queue = new LinkedList<>();
		queue.offer(sourceCell.coord);
		visited.add(sourceCell.coord);
		while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
			Coordinate current = queue.poll();
			if (current.equals(sinkCell.coord)) {
				return true;
			}
			Cell currentCell = cells[current.row][current.col];
			List<Direction> directions = new ArrayList<>();
			if (currentCell instanceof Pipe pipe) {
				directions.addAll(pipe.getConnectedDirections());
			} else if (currentCell instanceof TerminationCell termCell) {
				directions.add(termCell.getDirection());
			} else {
				continue;
			}
			for (Direction dir : directions) {
				Coordinate neighbor = current.add(dir.getOffset());
				if (isInBounds(neighbor) && !visited.contains(neighbor)) {
					Cell neighborCell = cells[neighbor.row][neighbor.col];
					boolean connected = false;
					if (neighborCell instanceof Pipe neighborPipe) {
						if (neighborPipe.getConnectedDirections().contains(dir.getOpposite())) {
							connected = true;
						}
					} else if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell neighborTerm) {
						if (neighborTerm.equals(sinkCell) && neighborTerm.getDirection() == dir) {
							connected = true;
						}
					}
					if (connected) {
						visited.add(neighbor);
						queue.offer(neighbor);
					}
				}
			}
		}
		return false;
	}
}

package game.map;

import game.map.cells.Cell;
import game.map.cells.FillableCell;
import game.map.cells.TerminationCell;
import game.map.cells.Wall;
import game.pipes.Pipe;
import io.Deserializer;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import util.Coordinate;
import util.Direction;
import util.StringUtils;

import java.util.*;

/**
 * Map of the game.
 */
public class Map {

	private final int rows;
	private final int cols;
	@NotNull
	final Cell[][] cells;

	private TerminationCell sourceCell;
	private TerminationCell sinkCell;

	@NotNull
	private final Set<Coordinate> filledTiles = new HashSet<>();
	private int prevFilledTiles = 0;
	private Integer prevFilledDistance;

	/**
	 * Constructs a map from a map string.
	 * <p>
	 * This is a convenience method for unit testing.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param rows     Number of rows.
	 * @param cols     Number of columns.
	 * @param cellsRep String representation of the map, with columns delimited by {@code '\n'}.
	 * @return A map with the cells set from {@code cellsRep}.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException If the map is incorrectly formatted.
	 */
	@NotNull
	static Map fromString(int rows, int cols, @NotNull String cellsRep) {
		var cells = Deserializer.parseString(rows, cols, cellsRep);
		return new Map(rows, cols, cells);
	}

	/**
	 * Constructor to initialize map with given size.
	 */
	public Map(int rows, int cols) {
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
				cells[r][c] = new FillableCell();
			}
		}
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sourceInfo = generateStartCellInfo();
		Coordinate sourceCoord = sourceInfo.coord;
		Direction sourceDirection = sourceInfo.direction;
		sourceCell = new TerminationCell(sourceCoord, sourceDirection, true);
		cells[sourceCoord.row][sourceCoord.col] = sourceCell;
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sinkInfo = generateEndCellInfo();
		Coordinate sinkCoord = sinkInfo.coord;
		Direction sinkDirection = sinkInfo.direction;
		sinkCell = new TerminationCell(sinkCoord, sinkDirection, false);
		cells[sinkCoord.row][sinkCoord.col] = sinkCell;
	}

	/**
	 * Constructor to initialize map with given size and cell array.
	 */
	public Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) {
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			System.arraycopy(cells[r], 0, this.cells[r], 0, cols);
		}
		sourceCell = null;
		sinkCell = null;
		int sourceCount = 0;
		int sinkCount = 0;
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
				Cell cell = this.cells[r][c];
				if (cell instanceof TerminationCell termCell) {
					if (termCell.isSource()) {
						sourceCount++;
						sourceCell = termCell;
						if (r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source must not be on edge");
						}
						Direction dir = termCell.getDirection();
						Coordinate nextCoord = new Coordinate(r, c).add(dir.getOffset());
						if (isInBounds(nextCoord)) {
							Cell nextCell = this.cells[nextCoord.row][nextCoord.col];
							if (nextCell instanceof Wall) {
								throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source cannot point into a wall");
							}
						}
					} else {
						if (r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1) {
							sinkCount++;
							sinkCell = termCell;
							Direction dir = termCell.getDirection();
							Coordinate nextCoord = new Coordinate(r, c).add(dir.getOffset());
							if (isInBounds(nextCoord)) {
								throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink must point outside the map");
							}
						}
					}
				}
			}
		}
		if (sourceCount != 1) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("There must be exactly one source cell");
		}
		if (sinkCount != 1) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("There must be exactly one sink cell");
		}
	}

	// ... rest of the class remains unchanged
}

package game.map;

import game.map.cells.Cell;
import game.map.cells.FillableCell;
import game.map.cells.TerminationCell;
import game.map.cells.Wall;
import io.Deserializer;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import util.Coordinate;
import util.Direction;
import util.StringUtils;

import java.util.*;

/**
 * Map of the game.
 */
public class Map {

	private final int rows;
	private final int cols;
	@NotNull
	final Cell[][] cells;

	private TerminationCell sourceCell;
	private TerminationCell sinkCell;

	@NotNull
	private final Set<Coordinate> filledTiles = new HashSet<>();
	private int prevFilledTiles = 0;
	private Integer prevFilledDistance;

	/**
	 * Constructs a map from a map string.
	 * <p>
	 * This is a convenience method for unit testing.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param rows     Number of rows.
	 * @param cols     Number of columns.
	 * @param cellsRep String representation of the map, with columns delimited by {@code '\n'}.
	 * @return A map with the cells set from {@code cellsRep}.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException If the map is incorrectly formatted.
	 */
	@NotNull
	static Map fromString(int rows, int cols, @NotNull String cellsRep) {
		var cells = Deserializer.parseString(rows, cols, cellsRep);
		return new Map(rows, cols, cells);
	}

	/**
	 * Constructor to initialize map with given size.
	 */
	public Map(int rows, int cols) {
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
				cells[r][c] = new FillableCell();
			}
		}
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sourceInfo = generateStartCellInfo();
		Coordinate sourceCoord = sourceInfo.coord;
		Direction sourceDirection = sourceInfo.direction;
		sourceCell = new TerminationCell(sourceCoord, sourceDirection, true);
		cells[sourceCoord.row][sourceCoord.col] = sourceCell;
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sinkInfo = generateEndCellInfo();
		Coordinate sinkCoord = sinkInfo.coord;
		Direction sinkDirection = sinkInfo.direction;
		sinkCell = new TerminationCell(sinkCoord, sinkDirection, false);
		cells[sinkCoord.row][sinkCoord.col] = sinkCell;
	}

	/**
	 * Constructor to initialize map with given size and cell array.
	 */
	public Map(int rows, int cols, @NotNull Cell[][] cells) {
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			System.arraycopy(cells[r], 0, this.cells[r], 0, cols);
		}
		sourceCell = null;
		sinkCell = null;
		int sourceCount = 0;
		int sinkCount = 0;
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
				Cell cell = this.cells[r][c];
				if (cell instanceof TerminationCell termCell) {
					if (termCell.isSource()) {
						sourceCount++;
						sourceCell = termCell;
						if (r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source must not be on edge");
						}
						Direction dir = termCell.getDirection();
						Coordinate nextCoord = new Coordinate(r, c).add(dir.getOffset());
						if (isInBounds(nextCoord)) {
							Cell nextCell = this.cells[nextCoord.row][nextCoord.col];
							if (nextCell instanceof Wall) {
								throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source cannot point into a wall");
							}
						}
					} else {
						if (r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1) {
							sinkCount++;
							sinkCell = termCell;
							Direction dir = termCell.getDirection();
							Coordinate nextCoord = new Coordinate(r, c).add(dir.getOffset());
							if (isInBounds(nextCoord)) {
								throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink must point outside the map");
							}
						}
					}
				}
			}
		}
		if (sourceCount != 1) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("There must be exactly one source cell");
		}
		if (sinkCount != 1) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("There must be exactly one sink cell");
		}
	}

Response Text:---
The task is to implement the main game loop inside the `start()` method, allowing players to take turns, making moves until a winner is determined. The loop should:

- Retrieve the list of players from `configuration.getPlayers()`.
- Cycle through players in order, allowing each to make a move via `nextMove()`.
- After each move, call `refreshOutput()`.
- Check for a winner after each move using `getWinner()`.
- When a winner is found, set `winner` and exit the loop.

Here's a complete implementation of the `start()` method:

```java
@Override
public Player start() {
    // reset all things
    Player winner = null;
    this.numMoves = 0;
    this.board = configuration.getInitialBoard();
    this.currentPlayer = null;
    this.refreshOutput();

    Player[] players = configuration.getPlayers();
    int currentIndex = 0;

    while (true) {
        Player currentPlayer = players[currentIndex];
        this.currentPlayer = currentPlayer;

        // Get available moves for current player
        Move[] moves = getAvailableMoves(currentPlayer);
        if (moves.length == 0) {
            // No moves available, skip turn or handle accordingly
            // For simplicity, assume game continues
            // Alternatively, could check for draw or end game
        }

        // Retrieve next move from the player
        Move move = currentPlayer.nextMove(this, moves);

        // Make the move
        movePiece(move);

        // Update score based on move
        Piece movedPiece = board[move.source().x()][move.source().y()];
        updateScore(currentPlayer, movedPiece, move);

        // Refresh output
        this.refreshOutput();

        // Check for winner
        Player potentialWinner = getWinner(currentPlayer, movedPiece, move);
        if (potentialWinner != null) {
            winner = potentialWinner;
            break;
        }

        // Prepare for next turn
        currentIndex = (currentIndex + 1) % players.length;
        this.numMoves++;
    }

    System.out.println();
    System.out.println("Congratulations! ");
    System.out.printf("Winner: %s%s%s\n", winner.getColor(), winner.getName(), Color.DEFAULT);
    return winner;
}
```

**Explanation:**

- Initializes game state.
- Loops indefinitely, cycling through players.
- For each player:
  - Retrieves available moves.
  - Gets the player's chosen move.
  - Executes the move.
  - Updates the player's score.
  - Refreshes the game display.
  - Checks for a winner.
- When a winner is found, exits the loop and returns the winner.

This implementation ensures the game proceeds turn-by-turn, respecting the order of players, and terminates upon a win condition.

The `getWinner` method should determine if the last move resulted in a winning condition. Since the specific game rules are not fully detailed here, a common approach is to check if the last move created a line of pieces (e.g., in a row, column, or diagonal) that meets the winning criteria. 

Assuming the game involves a grid and a player wins when they have a certain number of their pieces aligned (e.g., 3 or more in a row), the method should:

1. Identify the position of the last move.
2. Check in all directions (horizontal, vertical, diagonal) from that position for a consecutive sequence of the last player's pieces.
3. If such a sequence meets the winning condition, return the last player as the winner.
4. Otherwise, return null.

Below is a complete implementation assuming a typical line-based winning condition (e.g., 3 in a row). Adjust the `WIN_CONDITION` as needed for your specific game rules.

```java
@Override
public Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove) {
    // Define the number of consecutive pieces needed to win
    final int WIN_CONDITION = 3; // Adjust as per game rules
    
    // Get the position of the last move
    int x = lastMove.destination().x();
    int y = lastMove.destination().y();
    
    // Directions to check: horizontal, vertical, diagonal (\), anti-diagonal (/)
    int[][] directions = {
        {1, 0},  // horizontal
        {0, 1},  // vertical
        {1, 1},  // diagonal (\)
        {1, -1}  // anti-diagonal (/)
    };
    
    for (int[] dir : directions) {
        int count = 1; // Count includes the last placed piece
        
        // Check in the positive direction
        int dx = dir[0], dy = dir[1];
        int nx = x + dx, ny = y + dy;
        while (isValidPosition(nx, ny) && isPlayerPieceAt(lastPlayer, nx, ny)) {
            count++;
            nx += dx;
            ny += dy;
        }
        
        // Check in the negative direction
        dx = -dir[0];
        dy = -dir[1];
        nx = x + dx;
        ny = y + dy;
        while (isValidPosition(nx, ny) && isPlayerPieceAt(lastPlayer, nx, ny)) {
            count++;
            nx += dx;
            ny += dy;
        }
        
        // Check if count meets or exceeds the winning condition
        if (count >= WIN_CONDITION) {
            return lastPlayer;
        }
    }
    // No winner found
    return null;
}

// Helper method to check if position is within board bounds
private boolean isValidPosition(int x, int y) {
    return x >= 0 && y >= 0 && x < board.length && y < board[0].length;
}

// Helper method to check if the piece at (x,y) belongs to the given player
private boolean isPlayerPieceAt(Player player, int x, int y) {
    Piece piece = board[x][y];
    if (piece == null) {
        return false;
    }
    // Assuming Piece has a method getOwner() returning Player
    return piece.getOwner().equals(player);
}

Response Text:---
The `updateScore` method calculates the Manhattan distance between the move's source and destination places and adds this value to the player's current score. This aligns with the description that each move's score is based on the Manhattan distance, and the player's total score is the sum of all such move distances.

Here's the complete implementation:

```java
public void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move) {
    Place source = move.source();
    Place destination = move.destination();
    int distance = Math.abs(source.x() - destination.x()) + Math.abs(source.y() - destination.y());
    int currentScore = player.getScore();
    player.setScore(currentScore + distance);
}

```java
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
    ArrayList<Move> validMoves = new ArrayList<>();
    Piece[][] board = this.board; // Access the current game board
    for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
        for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
            Piece piece = board[x][y];
            if (piece != null && piece.getOwner().equals(player)) {
                Place currentPlace = new Place(x, y);
                // Get all moves suggested by the piece
                Move[] potentialMoves = piece.getAvailableMoves(this, currentPlace);
                for (Move move : potentialMoves) {
                    // Validate move: ensure move is within bounds and does not land on own piece
                    if (isValidMove(move, player)) {
                        validMoves.add(move);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    return validMoves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}

// Helper method to validate a move
private boolean isValidMove(Move move, Player player) {
    Place dest = move.destination();
    int x = dest.x();
    int y = dest.y();
    // Check if destination is within board bounds
    if (!isValidPosition(x, y)) {
        return false;
    }
    Piece targetPiece = board[x][y];
    // Check if destination is empty or occupied by opponent
    if (targetPiece != null && targetPiece.getOwner().equals(player)) {
        return false; // Cannot move onto own piece
    }
    // Additional validation can be added here if needed
    return true;
}

// Assuming isValidPosition is defined as:
private boolean isValidPosition(int x, int y) {
    return x >= 0 && y >= 0 && x < board.length && y < board[0].length;
}

		this.board = configuration.getInitialBoard();
		this.currentPlayer = null;
		this.refreshOutput();
		Player[] players = configuration.getPlayers();
		int currentIndex = 0;
		while (true) {
			Player currentPlayer = players[currentIndex];
			this.currentPlayer = currentPlayer;
			Move[] moves = getAvailableMoves(currentPlayer);
			if (moves.length == 0) {
			}
			Move move = currentPlayer.nextMove(this, moves);
			movePiece(move);
			Piece movedPiece = board[move.source().x()][move.source().y()];
			updateScore(currentPlayer, movedPiece, move);
			this.refreshOutput();
			Player potentialWinner = getWinner(currentPlayer, movedPiece, move);
			if (potentialWinner != null) {
				winner = potentialWinner;
				break;
			}
			currentIndex = (currentIndex + 1) % players.length;
			this.numMoves++;
		}
		System.out.println();
		System.out.println("Congratulations! ");
		System.out.printf("Winner: %s%s%s\n", winner.getColor(), winner.getName(), Color.DEFAULT);
		return winner;
	}

	@Override
	public Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove) {
		final int WIN_CONDITION = 3;
		int x = lastMove.destination().x();
		int y = lastMove.destination().y();
		int[][] directions = { { 1, 0 }, { 0, 1 }, { 1, 1 }, { 1, -1 } };
		for (int[] dir : directions) {
			int count = 1;
			int dx = dir[0], dy = dir[1];
			int nx = x + dx, ny = y + dy;
			while (isValidPosition(nx, ny) && isPlayerPieceAt(lastPlayer, nx, ny)) {
				count++;
				nx += dx;
				ny += dy;
			}
			dx = -dir[0];
			dy = -dir[1];
			nx = x + dx;
			ny = y + dy;
			while (isValidPosition(nx, ny) && isPlayerPieceAt(lastPlayer, nx, ny)) {
				count++;
				nx += dx;
				ny += dy;
			}
			if (count >= WIN_CONDITION) {
				return lastPlayer;
			}
		}
		return null;
	}

	public void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move) {
		Place source = move.source();
		Place destination = move.destination();
		int distance = Math.abs(source.x() - destination.x()) + Math.abs(source.y() - destination.y());
		int currentScore = player.getScore();
		player.setScore(currentScore + distance);
	}

	public void movePiece(Move move) {
		Place source = move.source();
		Place destination = move.destination();
		int srcX = source.x();
		int srcY = source.y();
		int destX = destination.x();
		int destY = destination.y();
		Piece movingPiece = board[srcX][srcY];
		board[destX][destY] = movingPiece;
		board[srcX][srcY] = null;
	}
}

    ConsolePlayer userPlayer = new ConsolePlayer("UserPlayer");
    RandomPlayer computerPlayer = new RandomPlayer("ComputerPlayer");
    
    // Construct the configuration with the user player first to ensure they move first
    Player[] players = new Player[] { userPlayer, computerPlayer };
    Configuration configuration = new Configuration(size, players, numMovesProtection);
    
    // Add initial pieces for the user player
    Knight userKnight = new Knight(userPlayer);
    configuration.addInitialPiece(userKnight, 0, 0); // Place at top-left corner
    
    // Add initial pieces for the computer player
    Knight computerKnight = new Knight(computerPlayer);
    configuration.addInitialPiece(computerKnight, size - 1, size - 1); // Place at bottom-right corner
    
    // Create and return the game instance
    return new JesonMor(configuration);
}

The task is to implement the `getAvailableMoves` method for the `Knight` class, which should generate all valid moves for a knight piece from a given position on the game board. The method must consider the knight's movement pattern, check boundary conditions, and validate each move using existing rules.

**Explanation:**
- The knight moves in an "L" shape: two squares in one direction and one square perpendicular.
- From the current position (`source`), generate all 8 potential moves.
- For each potential move:
  - Check if the move is within the game board boundaries.
  - Create a `Move` object with the source and target places.
  - Validate the move using the existing `validateMove` method.
- Collect all valid moves into a list and return as an array.

---

**Proposed implementation:**

```java
@Override
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
    ArrayList<Move> validMoves = new ArrayList<>();
    int[][] moveOffsets = {
        {2, 1}, {1, 2}, {-1, 2}, {-2, 1},
        {-2, -1}, {-1, -2}, {1, -2}, {2, -1}
    };

    int currentRow = source.getRow();
    int currentCol = source.getCol();

    for (int[] offset : moveOffsets) {
        int newRow = currentRow + offset[0];
        int newCol = currentCol + offset[1];

        // Check if new position is within game board boundaries
        if (game.getBoard().isWithinBounds(newRow, newCol)) {
            Place targetPlace = new Place(newRow, newCol);
            Move move = new Move(source, targetPlace);
            if (validateMove(game, move)) {
                validMoves.add(move);
            }
        }
    }

    return validMoves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}
```

**Note:** This implementation assumes that:
- `Place` has a constructor `Place(int row, int col)`.
- `game.getBoard().isWithinBounds(int row, int col)` correctly checks boundaries.
- The `validateMove` method is used to ensure move validity according to game rules.

This code will generate all valid knight moves from the current position, considering game rules and boundaries.

@Override
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
    ArrayList<Move> validMoves = new ArrayList<>();
    int[][] moveOffsets = {
        {2, 1}, {1, 2}, {-1, 2}, {-2, 1},
        {-2, -1}, {-1, -2}, {1, -2}, {2, -1}
    };

    int currentRow = source.getRow();
    int currentCol = source.getCol();

    for (int[] offset : moveOffsets) {
        int newRow = currentRow + offset[0];
        int newCol = currentCol + offset[1];

	 *
	 * @param game   the game object
	 * @param source the current place of the piece
	 * @return an array of available moves
	 */

		// TODO student implementation
		return new Move[0];
	}

	private boolean validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
		var rules = new Rule[] { new OutOfBoundaryRule(), new OccupiedRule(), new VacantRule(), new NilMoveRule(),
				new FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()), new KnightMoveRule(),
				new KnightBlockRule(), };
		for (var rule : rules) {
			if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
				return false;
			}
		}
		return true;
	}
}

public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {

**Approach:**

1. **Identify all possible directions:** up, down, left, right.
2. **For each direction:**
   - Traverse empty squares until hitting a piece or the boundary.
   - If no piece is encountered, the move is valid (move to empty square).
   - If a piece is encountered:
     - Continue traversing to find a second piece.
     - If the second piece is an opponent's piece and the first piece was a "screen," then capturing is valid.
3. **Create Move objects for each valid move.**
4. **Validate each move with `validateMove` before adding.**

Here's the complete implementation:

```java
@Override
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
    ArrayList<Move> moves = new ArrayList<>();
    int[][] directions = { {1, 0}, {-1, 0}, {0, 1}, {0, -1} }; // down, up, right, left
    int maxRow = game.getBoard().getNumRows();
    int maxCol = game.getBoard().getNumCols();

    for (int[] dir : directions) {
        int row = source.getRow();
        int col = source.getCol();

        boolean screenFound = false; // To track if we've encountered a screen piece
        boolean hasEncounteredPiece = false; // To prevent multiple captures in one direction

        while (true) {
            row += dir[0];
            col += dir[1];

            // Check boundary
            if (row < 0 || row >= maxRow || col < 0 || col >= maxCol) {
                break;
            }

            Place targetPlace = new Place(row, col);
            Piece targetPiece = game.getBoard().getPieceAt(targetPlace);

            if (targetPiece == null) {
                // Empty square
                if (!screenFound) {
                    // Valid move to empty square
                    Move move = new Move(source, targetPlace);
                    if (validateMove(game, move)) {
                        moves.add(move);
                    }
                } else {
                    // After a screen, moving to empty square is invalid for capture, but valid for move
                    // For cannon-like movement, moving after screen is valid if no capture
                    // But in Xiangqi, cannon can move over screen to empty squares
                    Move move = new Move(source, targetPlace);
                    if (validateMove(game, move)) {
                        moves.add(move);
                    }
                }
            } else {
                // Encountered a piece
                if (!screenFound) {
                    // First piece encountered - potential screen
                    screenFound = true;
                } else {
                    // Second piece encountered after screen
                    if (targetPiece.getPlayer() != this.getPlayer()) {
                        // Opponent's piece - can capture if the move is valid
                        Move move = new Move(source, targetPlace);
                        if (validateMove(game, move)) {
                            moves.add(move);
                        }
                    }
                    // Whether capture or not, stop after second piece
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
    }

    return moves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}
```

**Explanation:**

- The method iterates over four directions.
- It moves step by step, checking boundary conditions.
- It tracks whether a "screen" piece has been encountered.
- It adds valid moves to the list, considering the rules for movement and capture.
- It validates each move before adding.

This implementation ensures all valid moves for the Archer are considered, respecting the movement rules similar to the Xiangqi cannon.

	private boolean validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
		var rules = new Rule[] { new OutOfBoundaryRule(), new OccupiedRule(), new VacantRule(), new NilMoveRule(),
				new FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()), new ArcherMoveRule(), };
		for (var rule : rules) {

The method `validate` should check whether the move is a capture and whether it occurs within the first `numProtectedMoves` moves of the game. If both conditions are true, the move is invalid (return false); otherwise, it is valid (return true).

Response Text:---
The `validate` method should check whether the move for an Archer piece is valid according to the rules similar to a cannon in Chinese chess. Specifically, the Archer can move like a rook (any number of empty squares along a rank or file) but must jump over exactly one piece (the "screen") to capture an opponent's piece, or move without jumping if no capture is involved.

Here's a brief explanation:
- If the move is a capture (destination occupied by an opponent's piece), there must be exactly one piece between source and destination.
- If the move is a non-capture (destination empty), the path must be clear (no pieces in between).
- The move must be along a straight line (same row or same column).

Below is a complete implementation of the `validate` method:

```java
@Override
public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
    Object sourcePiece = game.getPiece(move.getSource());
    Object targetPiece = game.getPiece(move.getDestination());

    // Ensure the source is an Archer
    if (!(sourcePiece instanceof Archer)) {
        return true; // Not an Archer, rule not applicable
    }

    // Check if move is along a straight line
    int srcRow = move.getSource().getRow();
    int srcCol = move.getSource().getCol();
    int destRow = move.getDestination().getRow();
    int destCol = move.getDestination().getCol();

    if (srcRow != destRow && srcCol != destCol) {
        return false; // Not a straight line move
    }

    int countPiecesBetween = 0;

    if (srcRow == destRow) {
        // Moving horizontally
        int startCol = Math.min(srcCol, destCol) + 1;
        int endCol = Math.max(srcCol, destCol);
        for (int col = startCol; col < endCol; col++) {
            if (game.getPiece(move.getSource().withCol(col)) != null) {
                countPiecesBetween++;
            }
        }
    } else {
        // Moving vertically
        int startRow = Math.min(srcRow, destRow) + 1;
        int endRow = Math.max(srcRow, destRow);
        for (int row = startRow; row < endRow; row++) {
            if (game.getPiece(move.getSource().withRow(row)) != null) {
                countPiecesBetween++;
            }
        }
    }

    // Determine if move is a capture
    boolean isCapture = targetPiece != null;

    if (isCapture) {
        // For capture, exactly one piece should be between source and destination
        return countPiecesBetween == 1;
    } else {
        // For non-capture, path must be clear
        return countPiecesBetween == 0;
    }
}
```

**Note:** This implementation assumes that `move.getSource()` and `move.getDestination()` return objects with `getRow()` and `getCol()` methods, and that `game.getPiece()` can accept a position object or coordinate. Adjust accordingly if your classes differ.

Response Text:---
The method `validate` is intended to check whether a move involving a Knight piece in chess is valid according to specific rules. Since the comment indicates a "no block" rule, the typical validation for a Knight move involves ensuring the move follows the L-shape pattern and that the destination is either empty or occupied by an opponent's piece.

Here's a complete implementation of the `validate` method:

```java
@Override
public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
    if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Knight)) {
        return true; // Not a Knight move, so rule does not apply
    }

    int rowDiff = Math.abs(move.getDestination().getRow() - move.getSource().getRow());
    int colDiff = Math.abs(move.getDestination().getColumn() - move.getSource().getColumn());

    // Check for L-shape move: 2 in one direction and 1 in the other
    boolean isLShape = (rowDiff == 2 && colDiff == 1) || (rowDiff == 1 && colDiff == 2);
    if (!isLShape) {
        return false; // Invalid Knight move pattern
    }

    // Check if destination is occupied by own piece
    var destinationPiece = game.getPiece(move.getDestination());
    if (destinationPiece != null && destinationPiece.getColor() == game.getPiece(move.getSource()).getColor()) {
        return false; // Cannot capture own piece
    }

    // Move is valid
    return true;
}
```

**Explanation:**
- First, it confirms the piece at the source is a Knight.
- Then, it calculates the absolute difference in rows and columns between source and destination.
- It verifies the move follows the Knight's L-shape pattern.
- It checks if the destination is occupied by a friendly piece, invalidating the move if so.
- If all conditions are satisfied, it returns `true`, indicating a valid move.

This implementation ensures the Knight moves adhere to standard chess rules for Knight movement.

Response Text:---
The blocking rule for a Knight (or horse) in Chinese chess (Xiangqi) states that the Knight's move can be blocked if the "leg" position (the position immediately adjacent in the direction of the move) is occupied. To implement this, we need to determine the "leg" position based on the move's source and destination, then check if that position is occupied.

Here's the complete `validate` method implementation:

```java
@Override
public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
    if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Knight)) {
        return true;
    }

    int sourceRow = move.getSource().getRow();
    int sourceCol = move.getSource().getCol();
    int destRow = move.getDestination().getRow();
    int destCol = move.getDestination().getCol();

    int deltaRow = destRow - sourceRow;
    int deltaCol = destCol - sourceCol;

    // Determine the "leg" position based on move direction
    if (Math.abs(deltaRow) == 2 && Math.abs(deltaCol) == 1) {
        // Vertical move, check the intermediate row
        int legRow = sourceRow + (deltaRow / 2);
        int legCol = sourceCol;
        if (game.getPiece(new Place(legRow, legCol)) != null) {
            return false; // Blocked
        }
    } else if (Math.abs(deltaRow) == 1 && Math.abs(deltaCol) == 2) {
        // Horizontal move, check the intermediate column
        int legRow = sourceRow;
        int legCol = sourceCol + (deltaCol / 2);
        if (game.getPiece(new Place(legRow, legCol)) != null) {
            return false; // Blocked
        }
    }

    return true; // Not blocked
}
```

**Explanation:**
- Checks if the move is a Knight move (L-shape).
- Calculates the "leg" position based on move direction.
- If the "leg" position is occupied, the move is blocked, so return `false`.
- Otherwise, the move is valid, so return `true`.

This implementation correctly enforces the blocking rule for Knights in Chinese chess.

import assignment.protocol.Game;

/**
 * The blocking rule applying on Knights. The rule is similar to the blocking rule for horse in Chinese chess.
 *
 * @see <a href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiangqi#Horse'>Wikipedia</a>
 */
public class KnightBlockRule implements Rule {

The task is to implement the `nextMove` method for the `ConsolePlayer` class, which prompts the user for input, validates it, and returns a valid move from the available options. The implementation involves reading user input, parsing it into a `Move`, validating the move against the list of available moves, and handling invalid inputs by prompting again until a valid move is entered.

Here's a complete implementation:

```java
@Override
public Move nextMove(Game game, Move[] availableMoves) {
    Scanner scanner = new Scanner(System.in);
    while (true) {
        System.out.println("Enter your move (e.g., a1->b3):");
        String input = scanner.nextLine().trim();
        Move move = parseMove(input);
        if (move == null) {
            System.out.println("Invalid format. Please enter move in format 'a1->b3'.");
            continue;
        }
        // Check if move is among available moves
        boolean isValid = false;
        for (Move availableMove : availableMoves) {
            if (availableMove.equals(move)) {
                isValid = true;
                break;
            }
        }
        if (!isValid) {
            System.out.println("Move not available. Please choose a valid move from the list.");
            continue;
        }
        // Optional: validate move with game rules
        String validationMsg = validateMove(game, move);
        if (validationMsg != null) {
            System.out.println("Invalid move: " + validationMsg);
            continue;
        }
        return move;
    }
}
```

- Uses a `Scanner` to read user input from the console.
- Prompts the user repeatedly until a valid move is entered.
- Parses the input string into a `Move` object using `parseMove`.
- Checks if the parsed move is among the available moves.
- Validates the move according to game rules via `validateMove`.
- If all checks pass, returns the move; otherwise, prompts again.

This implementation ensures robust handling of user input and guarantees that the returned move is valid and available.

package assignment.player;

import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.piece.*;
import assignment.protocol.Color;
import assignment.protocol.Move;
import assignment.protocol.Place;
import assignment.protocol.Player;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

import java.util.Scanner;

/**
 * The player that makes move according to user input from console.
 */
public class ConsolePlayer extends Player {
	public ConsolePlayer(String name, Color color) {
		super(name, color);
	}

	public ConsolePlayer(String name) {
		this(name, Color.GREEN);
	}

	/**
	 * Choose a move from available moves.
	 * This method will be called by {@link Game} object to get the move that the player wants to make when it is the
	 * player's turn.
	 * <p>
	 * {@link ConsolePlayer} returns a move according to user's input in the console.
	 * The console input format should conform the format described in the assignment description.
	 * (e.g. {@literal a1->b3} means move the {@link Piece} at {@link Place}(x=0,y=0) to {@link Place}(x=1,y=2))
	 * Note that in the {@link Game}.board, the index starts from 0 in both x and y dimension, while in the console
	 * display, x dimension index starts from 'a' and y dimension index starts from 1.
	 * <p>
	 * Hint: be sure to handle invalid input to avoid invalid {@link Move}s.
	 * <p>
	 * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure the {@link Move} returned is valid.</strong>
	 * <p>
	 * <strong>Attention: {@link Place} object uses integer as index of x and y-axis, both starting from 0 to
	 * facilitate programming.
	 * This is VERY different from the coordinate used in console display.</strong>
	 *
	 * @param game           the current game object
	 * @param availableMoves available moves for this player to choose from.
	 * @return the chosen move
	 */
	@Override
	public Move nextMove(Game game, Move[] availableMoves) {
		// TODO student implementation
		return availableMoves[0];
	}

	private String validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
		var rules = new Rule[] { new OutOfBoundaryRule(), new OccupiedRule(), new VacantRule(), new NilMoveRule(),
				new FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()), new ArcherMoveRule(),
				new KnightMoveRule(), new KnightBlockRule(), };
		for (var rule : rules) {
			if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
				return rule.getDescription();
			}

			var piece = game.getPiece(move.getSource());
			if (piece == null) {
				return "No piece at " + move.getSource().toString();
			}
			if (!this.equals(piece.getPlayer())) {
				return "Cannot move a piece not belonging to you";
			}
		}
		return null;
	}

	private static Place parsePlace(String str) {
		if (str.length() < 2) {
			return null;
		}
		try {
			var x = str.charAt(0) - 'a';
			var y = Integer.parseInt(str.substring(1)) - 1;
			return new Place(x, y);
		} catch (NumberFormatException e) {
			return null;
		}
	}

	private static Move parseMove(String str) {
		var segments = str.split("->");
		if (segments.length < 2) {
			return null;
		}
		var source = parsePlace(segments[0].strip());
		if (source == null) {
			return null;
		}
		var destination = parsePlace(segments[1].strip());
		if (destination == null) {
			return null;
		}
		return new Move(source, destination);
	}
}

	/**
	 * Tries to move the player from a position in the specified direction as far as possible.
	 *
	 * <p>
	 * Note that this method does <b>NOT</b> actually move the player. It just tries to move the player and return
	 * the state of the player as-if it has been moved.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param position  The original position of the player.
	 * @param direction The direction to move the player in.
	 * @return An instance of {@link MoveResult} representing the type of the move and the position of the player after
	 * moving.
	 */
	@NotNull
	private MoveResult tryMove(@NotNull final Position position, @NotNull final Direction direction) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(position);
		Objects.requireNonNull(direction);

		final var collectedGems = new ArrayList<Position>();
		final var collectedExtraLives = new ArrayList<Position>();
		Position lastValidPosition = position;
		do {
			final Position newPosition = offsetPosition(lastValidPosition, direction);
			if (newPosition == null) {
				break;
			}

			lastValidPosition = newPosition;

			if (gameBoard.getCell(newPosition) instanceof StopCell) {
				break;
			}

			if (gameBoard.getCell(newPosition) instanceof EntityCell entityCell) {
				if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof Mine) {
					return new MoveResult.Valid.Dead(position, newPosition);
				}

				if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof Gem) {
					collectedGems.add(newPosition);
				} else if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof ExtraLife) {
					collectedExtraLives.add(newPosition);
				}
			}
		} while (true);

		if (lastValidPosition.equals(position)) {
			return new MoveResult.Invalid(position);
		}

		return new MoveResult.Valid.Alive(lastValidPosition, position, collectedGems, collectedExtraLives);
	}

	/**
	 * Offsets the {@link Position} in the specified {@link Direction} by one step.
	 *
	 * @param position  The original position.
	 * @param direction The direction to offset.
	 * @return The given position offset by one in the specified direction. If the new position is outside of the game
	 * board, or contains a non-{@link EntityCell}, returns {@code null}.
	 */
	@Nullable
	private Position offsetPosition(@NotNull final Position position, @NotNull final Direction direction) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(position);
		Objects.requireNonNull(direction);

		final var newPos = position.offsetByOrNull(direction.getOffset(), gameBoard.getNumRows(),
				gameBoard.getNumCols());

		if (newPos == null) {
			return null;
		}
		if (!(gameBoard.getCell(newPos) instanceof EntityCell)) {
			return null;
		}

		return newPos;
	}

If the move is invalid or results in the player's death, the game board should remain unchanged. The method will use the existing `tryMove` method to simulate the move, then apply the move if valid and safe.

Here's a complete implementation:

```java
public MoveResult makeMove(final Direction direction) {
    // Get the current player position
    Position currentPosition = gameBoard.getPlayerPosition();

    // Attempt to move the player in the specified direction
    MoveResult moveResult = tryMove(currentPosition, direction);

    // Check if the move is valid and the player is alive
    if (moveResult instanceof MoveResult.Valid.Alive) {
        MoveResult.Valid.Alive aliveResult = (MoveResult.Valid.Alive) moveResult;

        // Save the current state to revert if needed
        Position oldPosition = currentPosition;
        Position newPosition = aliveResult.getPosition();

        // Save previous cell states for potential undo
        Cell oldCell = gameBoard.getCell(oldPosition);
        Cell newCell = gameBoard.getCell(newPosition);

        // Move the player: update the game board
        gameBoard.setCell(oldPosition, new EmptyCell()); // Clear old position
        gameBoard.setCell(newPosition, new PlayerCell()); // Set new position

        // Collect gems and extra lives if any
        for (Position gemPos : aliveResult.getCollectedGems()) {
            gameBoard.removeEntityAt(gemPos);
        }
        for (Position lifePos : aliveResult.getCollectedExtraLives()) {
            gameBoard.removeEntityAt(lifePos);
        }

        // Return the move result
        return aliveResult;
    } else {
        // Invalid move or player died; do not mutate the game board
        return moveResult;
    }
}

	/**
	 * Tries to move the player from a position in the specified direction as far as possible.
	 *
	 * <p>
	 * Note that this method does <b>NOT</b> actually move the player. It just tries to move the player and return
	 * the state of the player as-if it has been moved.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param position  The original position of the player.
	 * @param direction The direction to move the player in.
	 * @return An instance of {@link MoveResult} representing the type of the move and the position of the player after
	 * moving.
	 */
	@NotNull
	private MoveResult tryMove(@NotNull final Position position, @NotNull final Direction direction) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(position);
		Objects.requireNonNull(direction);

		final var collectedGems = new ArrayList<Position>();
		final var collectedExtraLives = new ArrayList<Position>();
		Position lastValidPosition = position;
		do {
			final Position newPosition = offsetPosition(lastValidPosition, direction);
			if (newPosition == null) {
				break;
			}

			lastValidPosition = newPosition;

			if (gameBoard.getCell(newPosition) instanceof StopCell) {
				break;
			}

			if (gameBoard.getCell(newPosition) instanceof EntityCell entityCell) {
				if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof Mine) {
					return new MoveResult.Valid.Dead(position, newPosition);
				}

				if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof Gem) {
					collectedGems.add(newPosition);
				} else if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof ExtraLife) {
					collectedExtraLives.add(newPosition);
				}
			}
		} while (true);

		if (lastValidPosition.equals(position)) {
			return new MoveResult.Invalid(position);
		}

		return new MoveResult.Valid.Alive(lastValidPosition, position, collectedGems, collectedExtraLives);
	}

	/**
	 * Offsets the {@link Position} in the specified {@link Direction} by one step.
	 *
	 * @param position  The original position.
	 * @param direction The direction to offset.
	 * @return The given position offset by one in the specified direction. If the new position is outside of the game
	 * board, or contains a non-{@link EntityCell}, returns {@code null}.
	 */
	@Nullable
	private Position offsetPosition(@NotNull final Position position, @NotNull final Direction direction) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(position);
		Objects.requireNonNull(direction);

		final var newPos = position.offsetByOrNull(direction.getOffset(), gameBoard.getNumRows(),
				gameBoard.getNumCols());

		if (newPos == null) {
			return null;
		}
		if (!(gameBoard.getCell(newPos) instanceof EntityCell)) {
			return null;
		}

		return newPos;
	}

	public void GameBoardController(final GameBoard gameBoard) {
		this.gameBoard = Objects.requireNonNull(gameBoard);
	}
}

public void undoMove(final MoveResult prevMove) {
    if (!(prevMove instanceof MoveResult.Valid.Alive aliveMove)) {
        // If the move was invalid or resulted in death, no undo needed or handle accordingly
        return;
    }

    Position previousPosition = aliveMove.getPreviousPosition();

    gameBoard.setCell(previousPosition, new PlayerCell());

    }
}

Here's the corrected `Entity` class with the appropriate constructor:

```java
package pa1.model;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;

/**
 * An entity on the game board.
 */
public abstract class Entity implements BoardElement {

    @Nullable
    private EntityCell owner;

    /**
     * Default constructor initializing owner to null.
     */
    public Entity() {
        this.owner = null;
    }

    /**
     * Constructor accepting an EntityCell as owner.
     * @param owner the EntityCell to set as owner
     */
    public Entity(@Nullable EntityCell owner) {
        this.owner = owner;
    }

    /**
     * @return The {@link EntityCell} owning this entity, or {@code null} if this entity is not bound to a cell.
     */
    public final EntityCell getOwner() {
        return this.owner;
    }

    protected void Entity() {
        this.owner = null;
    }

    protected void Entity(final EntityCell owner) {
        this.owner = owner;
    }

    public final EntityCell setOwner(final EntityCell owner) {
        EntityCell previousOwner = this.owner;
        this.owner = owner;
        return previousOwner;
    }
}
```

This constructor allows subclasses or test code to instantiate `Entity` with an initial owner, resolving the compilation errors and test failures related to missing constructors.

    // Unset owner of previous entity if present
    if (previousEntity != null) {
        previousEntity.setOwner(null);

package pa1.model;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;

/**
 * A {@link Cell} on the game board which can contain an {@link Entity}.
 *
 * <p>
 * This class should observe and enforce the following constraints:
 * </p>
 * <ul>
 *     <li>There must be at most one entity owned by each cell; In other words, there should never be two entities'
 *     {@link Entity#getOwner()} pointing to the same {@link EntityCell}.</li>
 *     <li>There must be at most one cell owning each entity; In other words, there should never be two cells'
 *     {@link EntityCell#getEntity()} pointing to the same {@link Entity}.</li>
 * </ul>
 * <p>
 * More information is provided in the Javadoc of the methods in this class.
 * </p>
 */
public class EntityCell extends Cell {

	/**
	 * The entity which resides on this cell.
	 */
	@Nullable
	Entity entity = null;

	/**
	 * @return The entity currently present in this cell, or {@code null} if there is no entity present.
	 */
	public final Entity getEntity() {
		// TODO
		return null;
	}

	@Override
	public char toUnicodeChar() {
		return getEntity() != null ? getEntity().toUnicodeChar() : '.';
	}

	@Override
	public char toASCIIChar() {
		return getEntity() != null ? getEntity().toASCIIChar() : '.';
	}

	public void EntityCell(final Position position) {
		super(position);
	}

	public void EntityCell(final Position position, final Entity initialEntity) {
		super(position);
		if (initialEntity != null) {
			initialEntity.setOwner(this);
			this.entity = initialEntity;
		}
	}

	public Entity setEntity(final Entity newEntity) {
		Entity previousEntity = this.entity;
		if (previousEntity != null) {
			previousEntity.setOwner(null);
		}
		if (newEntity != null) {
			Entity previousOwner = newEntity.getOwner();
			if (previousOwner != null && previousOwner instanceof EntityCell) {
				((EntityCell) previousOwner).entity = null;
			}
			newEntity.setOwner(this);
		}
		this.entity = newEntity;
		return previousEntity;
	}
}

Response Text:---
The errors indicate that the code attempts to instantiate EntityCell objects using constructors like `new EntityCell(Position)` or `new EntityCell(Position, Entity)` which are not defined in the EntityCell class. This suggests that EntityCell does not have such constructors, or they are not accessible.

**Brief explanation:**  
To fix these errors, the code must use the existing constructors of EntityCell. Based on the provided EntityCell class, the only constructor explicitly defined is `public void EntityCell(final Position position, final Entity initialEntity)` which appears to be a method mistakenly named like a constructor. The actual constructor should be a proper constructor, e.g., `public EntityCell(final Position position)` or similar, but in the provided code, the constructor is incorrectly written as a method with a return type `void`. This is invalid in Java.

**Key fix:**  
- Correct the constructor in EntityCell to be a proper constructor:  
```java
public EntityCell(final Position position) {
    super(position);
}
```

- Ensure all instantiations of EntityCell use the correct constructors, e.g.,  
```java
new EntityCell(position) // if only position is needed  
// or with entity if constructor exists:  
new EntityCell(position, entity) // if such constructor exists
```

**Proposed corrected EntityCell class (only the constructor part):**  
```java
public class EntityCell extends Cell {
    @Nullable
    Entity entity = null;

    /**
     * Constructor for an empty EntityCell at a given position.
     */
    public EntityCell(final Position position) {
        super(position);
    }

    /**
     * Constructor for an EntityCell with an entity at a given position.
     */
    public EntityCell(final Position position, final Entity initialEntity) {
        super(position);
        this.entity = initialEntity;
        if (initialEntity != null) {
            initialEntity.setOwner(this);
        }
    }

    @Nullable
    public final Entity getEntity() {
        return this.entity;
    }

    // ... other methods ...
}
```

**Summary:**  
- Replace the invalid method-like constructor `public void EntityCell(...)` with proper constructor definitions.  
- Use these constructors in your code when creating EntityCell instances.  
- This change will resolve the compilation errors related to missing constructors and allow the tests and other code to instantiate EntityCell objects successfully.

package pa1.model;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;

/**
 * A {@link Cell} on the game board which can contain an {@link Entity}.
 *
 * <p>
 * This class should observe and enforce the following constraints:
 * </p>
 * <ul>
 *     <li>There must be at most one entity owned by each cell; In other words, there should never be two entities'
 *     {@link Entity#getOwner()} pointing to the same {@link EntityCell}.</li>
 *     <li>There must be at most one cell owning each entity; In other words, there should never be two cells'
 *     {@link EntityCell#getEntity()} pointing to the same {@link Entity}.</li>
 * </ul>
 * <p>
 * More information is provided in the Javadoc of the methods in this class.
 * </p>
 */
public class EntityCell extends Cell {

	/**
	 * The entity which resides on this cell.
	 */
	@Nullable
	Entity entity = null;

	/**
	 * @return The entity currently present in this cell, or {@code null} if there is no entity present.
	 */
	public final Entity getEntity() {
		// TODO
		return null;
	}

	@Override
	public char toUnicodeChar() {
		return getEntity() != null ? getEntity().toUnicodeChar() : '.';
	}

	@Override
	public char toASCIIChar() {
		return getEntity() != null ? getEntity().toASCIIChar() : '.';
	}

	public void EntityCell(final Position position) {
		super(position);
	}

	public void EntityCell(final Position position, final Entity initialEntity) {
		super(position);
		if (initialEntity != null) {
			initialEntity.setOwner(this);
			this.entity = initialEntity;
		}
	}

	public Entity setEntity(final Entity newEntity) {
		Entity previousEntity = this.entity;
		if (previousEntity != null) {
			previousEntity.setOwner(null);
		}
		if (newEntity != null) {
			Entity previousOwner = newEntity.getOwner();
			if (previousOwner != null && previousOwner instanceof EntityCell) {
				((EntityCell) previousOwner).entity = null;
			}
			newEntity.setOwner(this);
		}
		this.entity = newEntity;
		return previousEntity;
	}
}

```java
public EntityCell(final @NotNull Position position, final @Nullable Entity entity) {

/**

 */
public abstract class MoveResult {

	/**
	 * The {@link Position} of the player after moving.
	 */
	@NotNull
	public final Position newPosition;

	/**
	 * Represents a valid move.
	 */
	public static class Valid extends MoveResult {

		/**
		 * The original position of the player before the move.
		 */
		@NotNull
		public final Position origPosition;

		/**
		 * Creates an instance of {@link Valid}, indicating that the move is valid.
		 *
		 * @param newPosition  The new {@link Position} of the player after moving.
		 * @param origPosition The original {@link Position} of the player before moving.
		 */
		private Valid(@NotNull final Position newPosition, @NotNull final Position origPosition) {
			super(newPosition);

			this.origPosition = Objects.requireNonNull(origPosition);
		}

		/**
		 * Represents a valid move, and the player is alive after making the move.
		 */
		public static final class Alive extends Valid {

			/**
			 * List of positions representing the location of {@link Gem} collected in this move.
			 */
			@NotNull
			public final List<Position> collectedGems;
			/**
			 * List of positions representing the location of {@link ExtraLife} collected in this move.
			 */
			@NotNull
			public final List<Position> collectedExtraLives;

			/**
			 * Creates an instance of {@link Alive}, indicating that the move is valid and the player
			 * is still alive after the move.
			 *
			 * <p>
			 * {@link Alive#collectedGems} and {@link Alive#collectedExtraLives} will be initialized to an empty list
			 * using this constructor.
			 * </p>
			 *
			 * @param newPosition  The new {@link Position} of the player after the move.
			 * @param origPosition The original {@link Position} of the player before the move.
			 */
			public Alive(@NotNull final Position newPosition, @NotNull final Position origPosition) {
				this(newPosition, origPosition, Collections.emptyList(), Collections.emptyList());
			}

			/**
			 * Creates an instance of {@link Alive}, indicating that the move is valid and the player
			 * is still alive after the move.
			 *
			 * @param newPosition         The new {@link Position} of the player after the move.
			 * @param origPosition        The original {@link Position} of the player before the move.
			 * @param collectedGems       The list of positions of all gems collected in this move.
			 * @param collectedExtraLives The list of positions of all extra lives collected in this move.
			 */
			public Alive(@NotNull final Position newPosition, @NotNull final Position origPosition,
					@NotNull final List<Position> collectedGems, @NotNull final List<Position> collectedExtraLives) {
				super(newPosition, origPosition);

				this.collectedGems = Collections.unmodifiableList(Objects.requireNonNull(collectedGems));
				this.collectedExtraLives = Collections.unmodifiableList(Objects.requireNonNull(collectedExtraLives));
			}
		}

```java
public GameBoard(final int numRows, final int numCols, final Cell[][] cells) {
    // Validate dimensions
    if (cells.length != numRows) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Number of rows does not match cells array length");
    }
    if (cells.length == 0 || cells[0].length != numCols) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Number of columns does not match cells[0].length");
    }

    // Assign fields
    this.numRows = numRows;
    this.numCols = numCols;
    this.board = new Cell[numRows][numCols];

    // Copy cells to board
    for (int r = 0; r < numRows; r++) {
        if (cells[r].length != numCols) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("All rows must have the same number of columns");
        }
        System.arraycopy(cells[r], 0, this.board[r], 0, numCols);
    }

    // Find the single player
    Player foundPlayer = null;
    int gemCount = 0;
    for (int r = 0; r < numRows; r++) {
        for (int c = 0; c < numCols; c++) {
            Cell cell = this.board[r][c];
            if (cell instanceof EntityCell ec) {
                if (ec.getEntity() instanceof Player p) {
                    if (foundPlayer != null) {
                        throw new IllegalArgumentException("More than one player found");
                    }
                    foundPlayer = p;
                }
                if (ec.getEntity() instanceof Gem) {
                    gemCount++;
                }
            }
        }
    }

    if (foundPlayer == null) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("No player found");
    }

    if (gemCount == 0) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("No gems in the game board");
    }

    // Check reachability of all gems
    Position playerPos = null;
    for (int r = 0; r < numRows; r++) {
        for (int c = 0; c < numCols; c++) {
            Cell cell = this.board[r][c];
            if (cell instanceof EntityCell ec && ec.getEntity() instanceof Player p) {
                playerPos = p.getOwner().getPosition();
                break;
            }
        }
        if (playerPos != null) break;
    }

    if (playerPos == null) {
        throw new IllegalStateException("Player position not found");
    }

    List<Position> reachablePositions = getAllReachablePositions(playerPos);
    int reachableGems = 0;
    for (final var pos : reachablePositions) {
        Cell cell = getCell(pos);
        if (cell instanceof EntityCell ec && ec.getEntity() instanceof Gem) {
            reachableGems++;
        }
    }

    if (reachableGems != gemCount) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Some gems are unreachable");
    }

    // Assign final fields
    this.player = foundPlayer;
}
```

- The reachability check uses existing methods `getAllReachablePositions`.
- The constructor performs all validation as specified.

This implementation ensures the constructor initializes the `GameBoard` correctly, validating all constraints.

/**
 * The main game board of the game.
 *
 * <p>
 * The top-left hand corner of the game board is the "origin" of the board (0, 0).
 * </p>

public final class GameBoard {

	/**

	public GameBoard(final int numRows, final int numCols, final Cell[][] cells) {
		// TODO

		this.player = null;

	/**
	 * Checks that a single player exists on the game board, and returns the instance of the player.
	 *
	 * @return The single instance of player on the game board.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the game board has zero, or more than one player entities.
	 */
	@NotNull
	private Player getSinglePlayer() {
		Player player = null;
		for (final var row : board) {
			for (final var cell : row) {
				if (cell instanceof EntityCell ec && ec.getEntity() instanceof Player p) {
					if (player != null) {
						throw new IllegalArgumentException();
					}

					player = p;
				}
			}
		}

		if (player == null) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException();
		}

		return player;
	}

	/**
	 * Retrieves the instance of {@link EntityCell} by a position with an offset.
	 *
	 * @param pos    Position.
	 * @param offset Positional offset to apply.
	 * @return An instance of {@link EntityCell}, or {@code null} if the resulting position does not contain an entity
	 * cell.
	 */
	@Nullable
	private Position getEntityCellByOffset(@NotNull final Position pos, @NotNull final PositionOffset offset) {
		final var newPos = pos.offsetByOrNull(offset, getNumRows(), getNumCols());
		if (newPos == null) {
			return null;
		}
		if (getCell(newPos) instanceof Wall) {
			return null;
		}

		return newPos;
	}

	/**
	 * Gets all {@link Position} of cells which the player can stop on from the cell of the {@code initialPosition}.
	 *
	 * <p>
	 * A cell is "stoppable" iff the player can stop on the cell with any combination of valid moves.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param initialPosition The starting position to get all stoppable cells.
	 * @return {@link List} of all positions stoppable from {@code initialPosition}.
	 */
	@NotNull
	private List<Position> getAllStoppablePositions(@NotNull final Position initialPosition) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(initialPosition);

		final List<Position> allStoppablePos = new ArrayList<>();
		final List<Position> posToTraverse = new ArrayList<>();

		posToTraverse.add(initialPosition);

		while (!posToTraverse.isEmpty()) {
			final var nextPos = posToTraverse.remove(posToTraverse.size() - 1);

			if (!(getCell(nextPos) instanceof EntityCell)) {
				continue;
			}
			if (allStoppablePos.contains(nextPos)) {
				continue;
			}
			allStoppablePos.add(nextPos);

			for (@NotNull
			final var dir : Direction.values()) {
				for (int i = 0; i < Math.max(getNumRows(), getNumCols()); ++i) {
					final var posOffset = new PositionOffset(dir.getRowOffset() * i, dir.getColOffset() * i);
					final var posToAdd = getEntityCellByOffset(nextPos, posOffset);

					if (posToAdd == null) {
						final var maxDist = i - 1;
						if (maxDist > 0) {
							final var posOffsetBeforeThis = new PositionOffset(dir.getRowOffset() * maxDist,
									dir.getColOffset() * maxDist);
							final var posBeforeThis = getEntityCellByOffset(nextPos, posOffsetBeforeThis);

							if (posBeforeThis != null && !posToTraverse.contains(posBeforeThis)) {
								posToTraverse.add(posBeforeThis);
							}
						}

						break;
					}

					if (getCell(posToAdd) instanceof StopCell || isBorderCell(posToAdd, dir)) {
						posToTraverse.add(posToAdd);
					}
				}
			}
		}

		return Collections.unmodifiableList(allStoppablePos);
	}

	/**
	 * Gets all {@link Position} of cells which are reachable from the cell of the {@code initialPosition}.
	 *
	 * <p>
	 * A cell is reachable iff the player can move over the cell with any combination of valid moves.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param initialPosition The starting position to get all reachable cells.
	 * @return {@link List} of all positions reachable from {@code initialPosition}.
	 */
	@NotNull
	private List<Position> getAllReachablePositions(@NotNull final Position initialPosition) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(initialPosition);

		final List<Position> allReachablePos = new ArrayList<>();
		final List<Position> allStoppablePos = getAllStoppablePositions(initialPosition);

		for (@NotNull
		final var reachablePos : allStoppablePos) {
			for (@NotNull
			final var dir : Direction.values()) {
				for (int i = 0; i < Math.max(getNumRows(), getNumCols()); ++i) {
					final var posOffset = new PositionOffset(dir.getRowOffset() * i, dir.getColOffset() * i);
					final var posToAdd = getEntityCellByOffset(reachablePos, posOffset);
					if (posToAdd == null) {
						break;
					}

					if (!allReachablePos.contains(posToAdd)) {
						allReachablePos.add(posToAdd);
					}
				}
			}
		}

		return Collections.unmodifiableList(allReachablePos);
	}

	/**
	 * Checks whether the given cell is a border cell with reference to the direction.
	 *
	 * @param cellPos The position of the cell.
	 * @param dir     The direction is moving at.
	 * @return {@code true} if the cell at the specified position is a border cell, i.e. the last cell in the game board
	 * before going out of bounds in the given direction.
	 */
	private boolean isBorderCell(@NotNull final Position cellPos, @NotNull final Direction dir) {
		return switch (dir) {
		case UP -> cellPos.row() == 0;
		case DOWN -> cellPos.row() == getNumRows() - 1;
		case LEFT -> cellPos.col() == 0;
		case RIGHT -> cellPos.col() == getNumCols() - 1;
		};
	}

	/**
	 * Checks whether all gems are reachable from the player's initial position.

	 * @return {@code true} if all gems are reachable.

	private boolean isAllGemsReachable() {
		final var expectedNumOfGems = getNumGems();

		final var initialPosition = Objects.requireNonNull(getPlayer().getOwner()).getPosition();
		final var playerReachableCells = getAllReachablePositions(initialPosition);

		int actualNumOfGems = 0;
		for (final var pos : playerReachableCells) {
			final var cell = getCell(pos);
			if (cell instanceof EntityCell ec && ec.getEntity() instanceof Gem) {
				++actualNumOfGems;
			}
		}

		return expectedNumOfGems == actualNumOfGems;
	}

/**
 * The main game board of the game.
 *
 * <p>
 * The top-left hand corner of the game board is the "origin" of the board (0, 0).
 * </p>

public final class GameBoard {

	/**
	 * Number of rows in the game board.
	 */
	private final int numRows;
	/**
	 * Number of columns in the game board.
	 */
	private final int numCols;

	/**
	 * 2D array representing each cell in the game board.
	 */
	@NotNull
	private final Cell[][] board;
